bullets.title: NVDA: Blowout FY28 Guide +70% YoY; Wave of PT Raises from $285–$420
bullets.body: NVDA guided FY28 revenue growth ~70% YoY (vs. ~45% consensus) on agentic AI/factory demand, with Blackwell Ultra and Vera Rubin ramping; DC revenue +18% Q/Q in the July quarter. Wall Street responded with broad PT hikes: JPM $320 (from $280), Goldman $300 (from $285, though flagging range-bound near-term on elevated expectations), BofA $350 (Buy), Citi $315 (Buy, ~50% upside), Bernstein $400, Melius $420, Mizuho $315. Wolfe maintains Outperform at $275, noting $350B in purchase commitments (majority in first 3 years) and four novel financing structures de-risking revenue sustainability. Gross margins guided lower near-term (~71–73% in Jan Q) on higher memory costs before settling, but that overhang is now cleared; stock +7.2% premarket.

bullets.title: NVDA: AWS Orders 2M More GPUs; Hugging Face Acquisition for ~$13B; $500B Private Capital Platform
bullets.body: AWS committed to deploy 2M additional Blackwell Ultra, Rubin, and Rubin Ultra GPUs for 2027–2028. NVDA is reportedly acquiring Hugging Face for ~$12.9–13B (>85x trailing sales) to control the dominant open-source model repository and developer distribution — mirroring Microsoft's GitHub model. Separately, NVDA anchored a $500B private capital financing platform (Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman, KKR) to backstop AI data center capex, de-risking the $36B cloud capacity agreements starting FY29. Supply commitments doubled from $119B to $279B, primarily memory procurement through end of decade.

bullets.title: NVDA: Tariff Risk Emerging — White House Weighing Chips, Laptops, Servers
bullets.body: Politico reports the Trump administration is considering a new round of sweeping semiconductor tariffs, potentially expanding to laptops and servers and moving away from data center exemptions. This is an incremental risk to NVDA's supply chain and customer demand, though MS notes the broader tariff trajectory is still TBD. Policy could change and a phased implementation is also being considered.

bullets.title: CRWD: Record NNARR +51% YoY; FY27 ARR Growth Guide Raised 630bps; Citi/Goldman Raise PTs
bullets.body: CrowdStrike Q2 net new ARR $332.8M crushed the ~$300–305M estimate (+51% YoY vs +32% prior quarter); total ARR $5.84B (+25% YoY). FY27 NNARR growth guidance raised 630bps to +34% at midpoint; record Q3 pipeline at $345M. AI-driven security budget inflection accelerating faster than expected — AIDR ARR surging, Falcon Flex ARR doubled to $2.29B. Citi raises PT to $260 (from $250); Goldman raises to $230 (from $208); Evercore to $210. DA Davidson highlights CEO signaling larger M&A, SASE area of interest. Stock +9–10% on the day; 74% Buy, 24% Hold.

bullets.title: CRM: Agentforce ARR $1.5B (+240% YoY); DA Davidson Raises PT to $200; Opco to $275
bullets.body: Salesforce Q2 cRPO +14% YoY in constant currency; Agentforce + Data 360 ARR $3.9B (+210% YoY); net new annual order value strongest in 4 years. FY27 EPS raised +17.9%. However, organic revenue growth decelerated to ~6% YoY (vs. 8.7% prior quarter) and beat magnitudes narrowed for the 3rd consecutive quarter. Oppenheimer raises PT to $275 (Outperform); DA Davidson raises to $200 (Neutral); Citi raises to $233. 70% Buy consensus, average PT $254.

bullets.title: META: $18B Settlement Removes Legal Overhang; $10B/yr Anthropic Spend; EU Screen-Time Probe
bullets.body: Meta settled with 52 state AGs over social media addiction claims for up to $18B over 10 years, removing a major legal overhang. Separately, NYT reports Meta's internal projections show up to $10B/yr spend on Anthropic models to power internal tools and upcoming personal assistant 'Hatch.' The EU Commission also directed Meta to improve screen time management and parental controls. Citi remains bullish, noting Meta Connect on 9/23 as next catalyst. On financing, Meta is reportedly seeking to issue KRW-denominated bonds worth at least KRW 1 trillion in South Korea.

bullets.title: AVGO: Opco Initiates Outperform, $535 PT; F3Q Earnings Sep 2; ~10GW CY27 Locked
bullets.body: Oppenheimer initiates AVGO at Outperform with $535 PT, calling it the #2 AI chip player and #1 custom AI ASIC house (customers: Google, Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI). AI semi revenue modeled +215% YoY in F3Q and +250% in F4Q; management guided >$100B FY27 AI revenue. NVDA's ~70% CY27 DC guide expands the overall AI silicon TAM. AVGO trades at 18x CY27 EPS vs. AI peers at 31x; F3Q earnings due Sep 2 with the key watch being CY28 guidance. MS notes Vera Rubin ramp at $80B run rate nearly equals AVGO's entire AI semi business.

bullets.title: MDB: Hedgeye Adds as Top Long, $579 PT (~37% Upside); Atlas Growth 29%+ for 4 Qtrs
bullets.body: Hedgeye added MongoDB as a top long with a $579 12-18 month price target (stock at ~$423). Thesis: Atlas growth sustained at 29%+ for four consecutive quarters, platform attach among $100K+ customers rose from 37% to 45% (driven by Vector and text search), net ARR expansion +3pts off trough to 121%, and 34 consecutive quarters beating revenue guidance. Consensus models zero beat for FY27 despite company's historical beat rate. Risk: 2H FY27 Enterprise Advanced air pocket, MongoDB is the only major DB with negative usage growth on 2025 Stack Overflow survey.

bullets.title: OKTA: +21% on Biggest cRPO Beat in Five Quarters; AI Agents Optionality Unrealized
bullets.body: Okta's Q2 CRPO grew +14% YoY (vs Street ~11%), the biggest beat in five quarters, on improved sales productivity and IGA strength. FQ3 guidance implies ~14–15% growth. Okta for AI Agents signed a few dozen large deals but is not yet material. DA Davidson maintains Buy with $190 PT (32x EV/FY28 FCF); Citi raises PT to $165. OKTA hit a 52-week high, +22.6% on the day, +80% on a 52-week basis.

bullets.title: WSM: Beats Q2, Raises FY Guide; Morgan Stanley, RBC, KeyBanc, Telsey All Raise PTs
bullets.body: Williams-Sonoma Q2 revenue $1.96B (beat), comps +6.2% (vs. +4.5% est); all three brands beat consensus. FY revenue growth guide raised to +4.7–7.2%; operating margin guide raised to 17.8–18.2%. Tariff headwinds expected to ease in H2 (Q2 described as peak drag). Morgan Stanley raises PT to $240 (Eq-weight); RBC to $260 (OP); KeyBanc to $270 (OW); Telsey to $260 (OP). Sell-side 44% Buy / 44% Hold; avg PT +6% to $253.

bullets.title: DKNG: NFL Renews Multi-Year Partnership; Prediction Market Legal Overhang Could Clear
bullets.body: NFL announced multi-year official partnerships with DraftKings and FanDuel (partners since 2021), as well as a separate deal with Fanatics Betting & Gaming. More importantly, Mizuho notes DKNG is down 28% YTD largely due to prediction market (Kalshi/Polymarket) overhang, but recent court opinions are more favorable — if the overhang is removed, shares could move substantially higher. DKNG spending ~$300M in promotional spend this year.

bullets.title: FSLR: BMO Upgrades to Outperform, PT $263; Post-S232 Sell-off Seen as Overdone
bullets.body: BMO Capital Markets upgraded First Solar to Outperform from Market Perform, raising its PT to $263 (from $237), arguing the post-Section 232 tariff sell-off is overdone and the 2029+ booking window is favorable. BMO also views Tesla competitive risk as more than priced in. FSLR +3.7–4.5% in premarket.

bullets.title: COHR/ALAB/LITE/MTSI: AI Networking Supply Shortage Expected for 12-18+ Months
bullets.body: Jefferies semis conference takeaways: 1.6T transceiver optics demand tracking 100M units in 2027; COHR expects supply shortage for 12–18+ months and may need capacity expansion beyond its existing 4x plan. CPO adoption delayed to 2H 2028, creating near-term opening for NPO architectures. MTSI benefits from 1.6T demand and growing power delivery content. Management teams uniformly positive; supply — not demand — is the binding constraint for compute/networking.

bullets.title: PLTR: UBS Expert Call on SAP-Palantir Data Relationship (Sep 1)
bullets.body: UBS hosting a September 1 expert call with a 30-year SAP veteran (former Global VP Malcolm Woodfield) who has first-hand experience using Palantir in SAP upgrade cycles and cloud migration projects. Discussion will cover the interplay between SAP and data partners including Palantir and Databricks, and how the relationship may evolve — neutral framing but relevant for thesis around Palantir's enterprise data integration moat.

bullets.title: LRCX/AMAT: UBS Hosting CFO/IR Access at Semicon West Oct 12
bullets.body: UBS Research analyst Timothy Arcuri is hosting investor booth tours at Semicon West on October 12 in San Francisco, featuring LRCX CFO Doug Bettinger and AMAT IR/Corp VP Mike Sullivan. Notable access event for the semiconductor equipment group ahead of what Jefferies expects to be continued AI supply-driven capex.

bullets.title: AMD: Still Looks Constructive; Venice on N2 Could Deliver Acceleration
bullets.body: Jefferies semis conference notes AMD locked in substrate capacity during the pandemic, with potential YoY acceleration via Venice on N2. Separately, a trader on X flagged AMD chart looks strong, similar to TSM, with a recommendation to hold or buy dips. AMD also cited in unusual options volume context alongside Kodiak AI activity.

bullets.title: IREN/NBIS: AI Infrastructure Names Expected to Rally on Relief Bid Post-NVDA
bullets.body: Multiple sources flagging IREN and NBIS as AI infrastructure plays likely to benefit from the NVDA-driven relief rally, though authors expect the move to be short-lived given the macro backdrop. In premarket, HUT +4.6%, IREN +3.4%, CRWV +3.9% per pre-market summary.

bullets.title: TLN: Positively Levered to PJM Power Spreads; ERCOT Faces Policy Uncertainty
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley energy note highlights Talen Energy (TLN) as positively levered to PJM spark spreads, while ERCOT faces policy uncertainty and transmission timeline risk — a relative preference for the PJM-exposed power/data center nexus plays.

bullets.title: AVGO F3Q Earnings Sep 2 + AMBA Sep 3: Key Upcoming Catalysts to Watch
bullets.body: Per JPM macro week-ahead: AVGO reports F3Q earnings on September 2 (Oppenheimer initiated at $535 Outperform today). AMBA is scheduled to report earnings after market on September 3 with 215% unusual options volume per the options flow digest — worth monitoring for AI edge inference momentum. NFP prints Sep 4 at 8:30am ET; US-China AI talks planned for September; potential Xi visit Sep 24; META Connect Sep 23–24.

bullets.title: Semiconductor Tariff Risk: White House Weighing Broad Expansion Including Data Centers
bullets.body: Multiple sources (Politico via X, MS TMT note) flag the Trump administration is considering materially broader semiconductor tariffs, moving away from data center exemptions and potentially covering laptops and servers. MS TMT notes this as a key risk post-NVDA results. A phased implementation is also being considered. This is a sector-wide risk for NVDA, AMD, INTC, and downstream hardware names.
